etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English slaken (“to render slack, to slake”), from Old English sleacian, from Old English slæc (“slack”). Unrelated to, but possibly influenced by, the Old Norse sløkkva (“to extinguish”), compare Swedish släcka in the phrase släcka sin törst (“quench one's thirst”), släcka elden (“put out the fire”), and släckt kalk (“slaked lime”).
senses: (transitive) To cool (something) with water or another liquid. [from 14thc.]

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: Probably connected with Icelandic sleikja, "to lick", and German schlecken (“to lick”).
